Adding a subverse to the blocked set while subscribed to it keeps the subverse visible on front, but keeps it from being visible on all (as expected).

User expectation may not be so technical as to understand that blocked doesn't actually block the subverse, just exclude it from the v/all view. Otherwise, my front and all views are sometimes indistinguishable.

However, the argument could be made that when a user goes so far as to block a sub they typically mean they want it gone from their subscriptions too. This may be a potentially rare edge case considering the user would have had to subscribe to a subverse and then become disgusted enough to want it blocked.

For example: I have noted a few users saying they subscribed to v/pizzagate only to later block it. The UX issue would be potential confusion during the period of time a user blocks a subverse they no longer wish to see, while realizing the also have to unsubscribe from it to stop seeing the subverse in front and their "my subverses" list.

Ultimately the issue is one of communication: No single word terminology exists to explain the actual boolean logic of "blocked means the sub-verse will be excluded from your view of the v/all aggregate subverse". Therefore, "blocked" is used in a potentially ambiguous way.
